text: Anna Paola Concia, born on 4 July 1963, is an Italian politician and LGBT rights activist. She was born in Avezzano, Province of L'Aquila, and graduated in sports science from L'Aquila's Istituto Superiore di Educazione Fisica; after graduation, she worked as a physical education and tennis instructor. She first became involved in politics while at ISEF and was initially a member of the Italian Communist Party. In 1992, she moved to Rome following the death of her mother and the collapse of her marriage. She worked as a parliamentary assistant before serving as an adviser to Anna Finocchiaro, the minister responsible for equal opportunities, and later advised Giovanna Melandri after her appointment as Minister of Cultural Heritage and Activities in 1998. After the 2001 general election, Concia left politics to focus on her tennis career, and she came out as LGBT one year later. She was appointed as the Democratic Party's spokesperson on homosexuality and used this role to become a leading advocate for equal rights. She was first elected to the Chamber of Deputies in the 2008 general election. In August 2011, she married her wife, Ricarda Trautmann, in Frankfurt.
